stem: Which background feature should raise consideration of a vitamin-responsive neurological condition in a child?

options.text: Maternal dietary restriction or child dietary restriction
A history of open fontanelles in infancy

explanation: Maternal or child dietary restriction is the key background feature that should prompt consideration of a vitamin-responsive neurological condition.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: What Not to Miss in Neurology

optionExplanations.A: Correct because maternal dietary restriction or child dietary restriction is a recognised red flag for vitamin-responsive neurological conditions.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because parental handedness is not a relevant background feature for this diagnostic consideration.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because open fontanelles relate to infant skull assessment rather than vitamin-responsive neurological conditions.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because normal parental head circumference does not suggest a vitamin-responsive condition.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because previous cranial ultrasound does not address the dietary risk factor highlighted by this question.
